Usually metal units, time in ps. Rate 2.2 K/ps means temperature ramp per ps. If timestep is e.g., 0.001 ps (1 fs), then per timestep temperature increase = 2.2 K/ps * 0.001 ps = 0.0022 K per step. Could use "fix npt" with "temp/berendsen" or "temp/csvr" with "tstart tstop" and "Tdamp". LAMMPS allows "fix npt" with "temp start stop dtemp". Actually "fix npt" syntax: fix ID group-ID npt temp Tstart Tstop Tdamp iso Pstart Pstop Pdamp". So we can set Tstart 300 Tstop 2500 Tdamp something. The heating rate is controlled by Tdamp? Not exactly. The temperature will be ramped linearly over the simulation time if we set Tstart and Tstop and run for appropriate steps. Need to compute number of steps: heating from 300 to 2500 = 2200 K increase. Rate 2.2 K/ps => time needed = 2200 / 2.2 = 1000 ps. So total simulation time 1000 ps. With timestep 0.001 ps (1 fs), steps = 1,000,000 steps. That's large. But we can maybe use larger timestep like 0.002 ps (2 fs) => 500,000 steps. Still large. But we need to log every 1000 steps. units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p
read_data <structure_path>
replicate 3 3 3
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density

fix 1 all npt temp 300 2500 0.1 iso 0 0 1.0   # Tdamp 0.1 ps? typical 0.1 ps. Pdamp 1.0 ps.

timestep 0.001   # 1 fs

run 1000000   # 1,000,000 steps

write_restart melt.restart

We also need to output log file path. LAMMPS by default writes to screen and log.lammps? We can specify "log log.lammps". So include "log melt.log". Provide path.

Thus create script file e.g., melt.in.

Then run run_lammps with that script.
